description: Ten representative development records (April-May 2026) selected from the experiment manifests, with every quoted outcome tied to a git blob at the recorded commit. Rows describe single, uncontrolled runs; they are not controlled comparisons. Row 1 reports the September Measurement in place of the May figure, and row 9 adds the frozen 17-design record.

source.note: Manifests are read from git objects at this commit, so later working-tree edits do not change the record. Frozen data files are identified by SHA-256 under frozen_checks.

method.manifest_selection: Every tracked file matching experiments/<dir>/manifest.md or experiments/_archive/<dir>/manifest.md at the recorded commit, excluding experiments/_template/manifest.md.
method.status_rule: The first line beginning 'status:' inside the leading '---' YAML block; text after '#' is removed and whitespace stripped. The value is counted literally.
method.buckets: graduated, falsified, marginal and in_progress are counted as named; every other literal value is counted under other, with other_breakdown listing each value.
method.directory_rule: Experiment directories are the git tree directories directly under experiments/ and experiments/_archive/, excluding the _archive container and _template. experiments/_variance_check is untracked and therefore not counted.
method.hash_rule: manifest_blob is the git blob SHA-1 at the recorded commit; it equals `git hash-object` of an unmodified working-tree file.
method.status_caveat: The status field records the last value someone wrote. Development stopped on 22 May 2026, so many manifests were never closed: for example E84 (verified 17-design cascade, 11 May) and E117 (17-design record, 20 May) are still in_progress, and E65 (a negative structural finding) is graduated. Verdicts in rows therefore come from each manifest's outcome text, not from the status field.
method.selection_rule: Rows were chosen to tell the development story to a non-specialist and to mix kept and dropped ideas. Each candidate was checked against its manifest; candidates without a verifiable manifest were excluded (see excluded_candidates).
method.command_notes: The default command verifies every computed field against git objects and the frozen data files, then renders. --freeze COMMIT recomputes those fields from the git objects at COMMIT (default HEAD); working-tree edits are reported but never read.

table_caption: What we tried during development (Historical). Each row summarizes single-run development records from April–May 2026. The runs are uncontrolled: hardware, time budget and concurrency varied, and most comparisons are against a separate reference run. Scores are proxy scores; lower is better. Row 1 gives the September re-measurement (Measurement) in place of the May figure.

rows.plain_idea: Rescore only what a one-block move changes, instead of recomputing the whole score
rows.what_happened: September re-measurement on two designs: 1.3–3.7 ms per move versus 1.4–26.9 s for a full rescore; largest relative difference $2.6\times10^{-15}$.

scope.designs: May: IBM01 and IBM10, 130 random moves. September Measurement: IBM01 and IBM10, 14 distinct moves repeated in 2-3 batches.
scope.budget: Component evaluation only; setup and overlap checks excluded in the September measurement.
scope.runs: May: one benchmark run. September: paired batches.

rows.discrepancy: The May manifest reports a 4,657x speedup on IBM10 (6.5 ms per move versus 30 s). The frozen September microbenchmarks give 1.29-3.67 ms per move versus 1.40-26.87 s, median paired ratios of about 1,040x (IBM01), 7,269x (IBM10 soft-cluster moves) and 18,023x (IBM10 hard-macro moves). The table uses the frozen measurement. The May parity figure (worst absolute difference 1.1e-15 on 130 moves) is consistent with the frozen maximum relative component difference of 2.6e-15.

scope.runs: One run per design; no frozen per-design record.

rows.notes: The 69% figure is 17,480 s / 10,316 s from the manifest table. Part of the gain is therefore extra time on hard designs, which was the point of the stopping rule.

quoted_outcome_lines.text: fast_outcome: 0.9254 (--fast); +0.36 % vs E41 fast 0.92178; +0.56 % vs E48 fast 0.9202. Per-bench ibm01=0.9143, ibm04=0.9912, ibm09=0.8451, ibm13=0.9511. Across 4 benches, **DPO-basin phase contributed 0 accepts in 350 total restarts** (ibm01 0/121, ibm04 0/104, ibm09 0/72, ibm13 0/53). 600 s/bench × 4 of GPU MPS work (76 % of phase 7 wall) returned exactly zero proxy improvement. The −2.16 % lift seen on shortened-budget smoke (40 s CD/LNS/SA budgets, ibm01 1.0361 → 1.0137) does not reproduce at production budgets.

outcome: falsified — the basin-hopping mechanism (LNS-destroy + GPU-DPO-settler) does NOT find lift on top of fully-converged CD-LNS-SA. Smooth-proxy gradient cannot escape the local optimum that breakpoint enumeration + grid-bin LNS + breakpoint Metropolis already reach.

A September audit found that some competition-era smooth components ignored hard-macro pins on ariane133; whether this pipeline's initializer was affected was not checked, and the reference used the same components.

quoted_outcome_lines.text: fast_outcome: 0.9222 (--fast); tied with E41 0.92178 and E48 0.9202 within run noise. Compositional best-of-{E25,E41,E54} = 0.91708 (-0.31% vs E48), but best-of-{E48, E52 E41-seed1, E53_multiseed, E54} only -0.04% better than E53_multiseed alone — E54 contributes near-zero on top of multiseed.

ng45_outcome: **0.7022 (--ng45); +1.45 % REGRESSION vs E48 NG45 0.6922; ariane133 +5.14 % catastrophic loss (0.7214 vs E48 0.6861, E41 0.6733)**. Same NG45 failure pattern as E42 K=4 and E43 longer-K-joint. ariane136/mempool_tile/nvdla tied or near-tied; ariane133 alone dominates the regression. Congestion-targeted destroy is IBM-aware and NG45-blind on ariane-class designs.

all_outcome: **1.08568 (--all); +0.39 % vs E48 1.08151; +0.40 % vs E53_multiseed 1.08128.** Wall 52334 s = 14.5 hr (under heavy contention). E48 wins per-bench on 7 (ibm01, ibm03, ibm04, ibm06, ibm07, ibm10, ibm17 — biggest gap ibm01 −2.04 %); E54 wins on 3 (ibm02, ibm12, ibm16 by −0.10 to −0.13 %); 7 tied. Best-of-{E48, E54} = 1.08126 (only −0.023 % vs E48 — trivial). Confirms standalone E54 --all is slightly worse than E48 and adds nearly zero as a 3rd hybrid lane. Combined with NG45 +1.45 % regression, E54 is comprehensively falsified.

rows.plain_idea: Blend two good but different placements by moving every block partway along a straight line between them
rows.what_happened: On 2 designs, none of the 9 intermediate blends could be made overlap-free by the 50-iteration repair step; before repair, blends scored up to 61% worse.

scope.budget: Eleven evenly spaced points from one endpoint to the other; overlap projection capped at 50 iterations.

rows.notes: The manifest status is graduated because the result was filed as a structural finding; the verdict here refers to blending as a search method. The manifest's broad 'RULES OUT' wording rests on two cross-sections and a 50-iteration repair cap, so the table states only what was measured.

records.outcome_verbatim: Two cross-sections (ibm01, ibm12) both deliver MONOTONE-UP verdict with 0/9 feasible interpolations.

quoted_outcome_lines.text: outcome: **STRUCTURAL FINDING graduated 2026-05-03 02:01 EDT — INFEASIBILITY WALL between SDF and DPO basins is universal.** Two cross-sections (ibm01, ibm12) both deliver MONOTONE-UP verdict with 0/9 feasible interpolations. Wall is a function of spatial-configuration distance, not proxy distance — ibm12 endpoints differ by only 0.2 % in proxy yet are separated by a 233-residual wall. Confirms E61 V1 50/50 crossover failure (136 residuals) was geometric. **RULES OUT**: interpolation/crossover/local-move bridging of basins. **LEAVES AS BREAKTHROUGH OPTIONS**: (1) constructing structurally new third basin from scratch (E63 spectral, E40 BP, E43 diffusion sampling) — bypass the wall by not starting from either basin; (2) non-local feasibility-respecting moves like K=50 Hungarian re-pack — orders of magnitude beyond E41 K=3; (3) constrained NEB on the feasible manifold — active-set or barrier methods on the no-overlap-respecting region.
**Verdict: MONOTONE-UP with infeasibility wall.** 9 of 11 interpolation
points are *infeasible* (88-155 residual overlaps each) — they are not
just higher proxy, they are not feasible placements at all under the
50-iter legalization budget. The 2 feasible points are exactly the

quoted_outcome_lines.text: outcome: **MARGINAL 2026-05-03 23:00 EDT.** SP encoder works (Murata-Fujiyoshi adjacency rule, after fixing initial pair-by-pair over-constraint). Topology distance probe quantifies basin separation: 17-30% of pairs disagree across 4 IBM benches; most disagreements are axis-rotating (LEFT↔BELOW etc.) with only 7-15% axis-preserving. SP-guided directed swap on axis-preserving disagreements ALWAYS finds genuine lift over starting basin (-0.04% to -0.19%) but aggregate --fast lift (~-0.10%) is BELOW the 0.30% promotion threshold. Per-pair operations are too local to escape basin; block-level operations (E61 V2 quadrant crossover, -0.07% --all) outperform per-pair (E69) on tied-basin benches. **Validates the topology framing as REAL** but **falsifies per-pair swap as a breakthrough mechanism**. Real escape requires operations that scale (block-level, Hungarian K=50, BP/diffusion).

chronology_table.label: tab:chronology
chronology_table.caption: Glossary and development chronology (Historical). Dates (2026) are decision or commit dates; manifest gives the first seven characters of the experiment manifest's git blob, and runtime archive names are prefixes of each archive's source-identity SHA-256. Scores are mean proxy over the 17 IBM designs unless stated (lower is better); frozen values are recomputed from the saved records in the publication data. The judged commit was not recorded: from the listed 12-minute runtime and the 20 May resubmission date, the single pipeline (V4+Gaussian) is inferred to be the ranked entry, so Lanes A, B and C and the three-lane system, all committed before the deadline, are inferred never to have been scored.
